title: muse.tokens.consumed payload
description: The `data` payload of the `muse.tokens.consumed` event: one routed completion, metered. Exactly five fields, because a payload schema is closed and a field added now is one a future schema carries forever. There is no account, no request id and no price: muse's v1 auth stub does not read a token, so the envelope's `subject` is core's reserved literal `platform`, and a consumer cannot attribute this spend to a customer yet — see D9. The envelope is validated by schemas/event-envelope.schema.json; this schema validates what is inside `data`. The file path is the event type with dots as directory separators. See docs/event-naming.md.

model.description: The vendor's model id that actually answered — not the route name the client asked for. They usually differ, and sending the route name to a vendor is a 404.

provider.description: The provider that served the call, e.g. `openai` or `anthropic`. The client never learns which one ran; this is the record that it did.

tokens_in.description: Prompt tokens billed for this completion. Zero is legal — a cached prefix can bill no prompt tokens — and negative is refused by the publisher rather than rounded.

tokens_out.description: Completion tokens billed for this completion.

cost_micros.description: The cost of this completion in micro-dollars — integer, like every other amount in anywaye, and never recomputed downstream from a price table that may have moved since the call was priced. A consumer that re-derives it and disagrees has found a real bug, which is why the figure travels.
